title: Chapter 1081
paragraphs: Chapter 1081
Episode 254. The Egos of the Sun God (5)
Nepdol and Bligiet's words were true.

Vahn also agreed with their opinion and closed her eyes with a sorrowful face. For Dante to face the onslaught of Kragos and the Zipfel alone meant that a life-threatening danger would come for him second by second.
“Damn it! Hey, you Sun Gods. Is there really no way! For real? We just have to stand by and watch that weakling get killed by them?”
Murakan shouted in an agitated voice. To him as well, Dante was no longer just 'the kid's friend,' but a companion.

Dante was not a person precious only to Jin. To the people of the Empire, he was a regent, but a more than perfect, virtuous king, and to everyone in the coalition, he was the Sword Emperor they could always rely on.
[...It can't be helped. Malugia's power is absolute. Even if you were to release our restraints, we wouldn't be of much help.]
“For now, I'll keep tracking the records. While confirming Lord Dante's life or death, I'll try to find even the smallest clue that could be a lead.”
Jin could not properly hear what they were saying.
'Dante... is going to die? So... meaninglessly?'

Even with the senses he had gained upon reaching the state of a Genesis Knight, it was not easy to control his heart, which was beating as if it would explode. It felt as if his ears had stopped working, and as if he couldn't breathe, submerged in water.
“Brother Jin!”
“Kid, no. The demonic transformation is coming!”

Valeria, fearing that, had deliberately not mentioned the record of the Empire's citizens being annihilated in an instant. On the blue record screen, a number that felt unreal was continuously being updated.
However, there was no way Jin wouldn't know of that tragedy. Anyone would know.

The repeated massacres by the Zipfel, the calamity that had once again befallen the Empire which had suffered deep and great tragedies several times in the past, and on top of that, the fate of his friend who would die fighting alone in the midst of it all.
All of that was trying to sever the line that was being precariously maintained within Jin.
The emotions he had always barely managed to push aside, saying that atonement comes after everything is over—the rage, hatred, guilt, and madness—were about to surge to the surface.
What was driving Jin even more insane was this.

That there was nothing he could do right now. For the people who died in there, for the people who were dying, for his friend, there was nothing he could do. Even after creating the Vamel Alliance, liberating Lafrararosa, and building such a great force.
Jin had to make a choice.

It was the choice to exclude Dante. To bring all the forces of the coalition for a friend who would, with absolute probability, meet his death was of course a choice that he as the leader had to avoid.
On his single decision, the lives of tens, hundreds, thousands of millions of people crossed between life and death.
If Vahn were to unfold the Plutonian Domination Sword for a whole day for Dante, and all the superhumans and fleets of the coalition were to break through Malugia's golden wall.

What would happen after that was all too clear. As predicted, Dante would be killed in action, and the coalition, having suffered great damage, would once again be dragged around by the hands of their enemies.
'How... how do I... suppress this. How in the world.'
The heavy duty as the leader of the Vamel Alliance and the responsibility as the sole regressor would, this time as well, lead Jin to a rational choice.
However, before being the leader of the Vamel Alliance, he was, in essence, a single human being.
There was bound to be a moment where... a single beloved person felt more precious than the many whose lives depended on his decision.
That moment was now.
Whether he could save Dante or not, the impulse to pour in his and the Vamel Alliance's full strength was stabbing at his insides like an awl.
“Jin! Hey, Jin!”
Smack-!
Suddenly, someone struck Jin on the head. Veradin, he grabbed the shoulders of Jin, who had raised his head, and shook him wildly as he continued.

“You idiot, don't you get it!? Dante must have seen the people of the Empire dying in there with his own two eyes. He would have wanted to fight. He would have wanted to just fight and die! But he's still alive, not dead.”
“Veradin.”

“What do you think that means? That guy is running away. Because that's the right thing to do. Because if he fights carelessly before reinforcements arrive, he'll only lose his forces! It's the same for us, Jin. We have to fall back. Dante... Dante...”
Blood flowed from between Veradin's lips. He had been unknowingly biting his tongue and gritting his teeth the whole time he was speaking.

“Dante would want us to do that if he knew this situation. Because that's the right thing to do. Because he'd think that the world shouldn't be endangered because of wasted strength on his account! That guy only knows how to do the right thing... so get a grip. If you waver, the world is over. There's no one to replace you, you hear me?”
Tears flowed from Jin's two eyes. Veradin was barely holding back his own bursting tears.
“...All fleets, cancel assembly. The Empire... will not be supported. Everyone, the next... the next... prepare for the next battle.”
The line did not break, but sank into the deep wound that had just been carved into Jin's inner self.

Those who received the communication lowered their heads. The personnel of the Empire who were stationed in the Garden of Swords and Tikan collapsed and sobbed, and not a few fainted. Dante was beyond being a pillar of the Empire; he was as good as the Empire itself now.
Beeep...!
Jin squeezed his eyes shut at the feeling of something bursting in both his body and his inner self, along with the encroaching tinnitus.
Soon, after putting down the communicator, Jin stared at the golden wall with empty eyes. The image of his friend who must be beyond that wall, his face, would not form in his mind.
“Valeria, the records... please keep tracking them. We need to know what happened to be able to respond later.”
Tears were also welling up in the eyes of Valeria, who silently nodded without looking back.

-[The feeling of a companion, a comrade in arms, dying. Even a guy with as much experience as me can't get used to it. And it's not like Kragos is the only enemy... In the worst case, we might have to face the Tower of Stories or even Malugia and Araxion.]
Jin was recalling what Orgal had said a little while ago. As he had said, he could never get used to this sorrow.
[...Jin. This may not be a comfort, but. You all are not monsters because you can feel sadness.]
Nepdol said as she took Jin's hand. She and Bligiet felt a sense of debt as creators to Jin and everyone in the coalition. The debt of having made the world such a painful place.
Jin's gaze remained fixed on the golden wall.
[No matter how strong, no matter how great, if you cannot feel sadness at anything. You would not be much different from us before we realized, or those horrific mortals... huh?]
Nepdol suddenly cut off her words and blinked her eyes.
[Nepdol, this is!]
At the same time, Bligiet also raised his head as if he had sensed something. Only the egos of the Sun God were aware of the change that had just occurred on the battlefield.
Another ego of the Sun God was approaching this place from somewhere.
“What is it? Nepdol, Bligiet. Don't tell me another ego of the Sun God has come!?”

Right after Murakan shouted, Jin and the coalition were able to confirm the sight of a massive dimensional gate of a form they had never seen before opening between the flagship Sarah and the golden wall.
[Focal! This is Focal! Focal has come here! Kkyu!]
[Focal...!]

-The name of the ego of Kinzelo sleeping in that altar is Focal. He is an ego who wishes for the maintenance of the world. The Zipfel have used him as a material for the Origin Stone before. When he awakens, he will become a reliable ally of the coalition.
Words that Silkia Arcia had said in the Milla Kingdom not long ago.
From that day, the Demon Realm had received the Sun Sword Tetallon from Jin and had been preparing to awaken Focal. And today, they had succeeded.
“Jin! Jin! We're here! Silkia woke Lord Focal! Lord Focal said the situation was bad, so we came super fast, with Silkia and Lord Focal's power.”
“Jin, are you alright!”
“Sir Jin!”
The voices of Misol, Tilias, and Silkia, his companions from the Demon Realm, were heard. They were flying in the sky, wrapped in the newly appeared Sun energy on the battlefield.
And behind the three of them, the figure of Focal, who was the last to emerge from the dimensional gate, could be seen. She had a human-like form like Kragos, and her build was very small.
However, that small body held the infinite benevolence of a creator who loved this world.
[Pitiful mortal, you were lost in sorrow.]
Focal instantly approached Jin and met his eyes. The moment Jin looked into her eyes, he felt as if his inner sorrow was being washed away.
His vision, which had been blurred with tears, was now becoming clear.

Soon, Focal embraced Jin, and beyond the bridge, the sight of the dimensional gate she had emerged from closing and the golden wall melting away could be seen. It was a wall that was said to require at least a day to destroy even if all the forces of the coalition were to attack.
The egos of Maintenance were, naturally, the beings who most strongly opposed the egos of destruction. And among them, Focal was the only ego who could, to some extent, single-handedly stop Malugia.
[Go and cut down your sorrow. I am one who exists to protect the world. I shall lend you my strength.]
Focal had already released Jin from her embrace and was sending him flying along the path she had opened. Like melting snow, the golden walls were ceaselessly crumbling away.
[Let's go, Vahn!]
Murakan, Vahn, and the flagship Sarah also began to advance along the path Focal had formed.
It did not take long to reach the Imperial Capital where Dante was fighting alone. Every time the golden wall crumbled, Focal and Silkia closed the distance and opened a new dimensional gate.
“Dante!”
After crossing five dimensional gates in just over ten seconds, Jin was able to stand next to Dante, who was in tatters on the half-destroyed Sword Emperor's Ship, barely holding up his sword.
“Jin... Jin? Is that really you? Am I seeing things?”
“Dante, you bastard! This damn, damn it, I'm sorry! I'm sorry!”
Veradin and the companions, who had arrived at almost the same time, also took their positions by Dante's side. Jin placed a hand on Dante's shoulder and said.
“You can rest now, Dante. Thank you, for being alive.”
He had saved his friend. Now, it was time for the people's revenge.
